confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly uses a randomized between-subjects design: "The quantitative phase deployed a randomized between-subjects experimental design with three conditions:" The abstract independently calls the three experimental conditions randomized; this evidence is separate from the random-sampling description.

confirmed.statement: The conditions apply to student participants producing their own creative work: alternative solutions and a conceptual campaign brief. The manipulation concerns their access to assistance, rather than which source of output an evaluator sees.

confirmed.statement: The structured arm used the same LLM interface under CARP: at least three independent ideas before opening it, critique and counter-factual prompts, then synthesis and divergent expansion without copying generated text. The comparison between the two AI arms therefore changes the assistance protocol, as coded.

confirmed.statement: The design is between subjects, so randomized condition order is inapplicable. The fixed unaided-to-AI sequence within CARP is an intervention component, not a within-person comparison of the three experimental conditions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Section 3.1, design statement and Condition 3, Phases A-C.

summary: The document explicitly reports a randomized between-subjects experiment comparing unaided work, unconstrained LLM access, and structured use of the same LLM interface. S1's assignment and assistance coding are supported, so criterion 1 holds.
